label: Befindlichkeit + Temporal Divergence
sections: 2.1 I. Befindlichkeit: The Primordial Structure of Attunement
2.2 II. The Temporal Divergence: Aisthesis and Stimmung
main_themes: Stimmung as existential structure (not psychological state)
Befindlichkeit: how-one-finds-oneself, prior to any particular mood
aisthesis vs Stimmung comparison: instantaneous contact vs pervading temporality

tables.title: Aisthesis vs Stimmung Comparison
rows: Occurs only at the instant of contact
Disappears instantly when object is gone
Is not tied to a single instant
Shapes our entire horizon of meaning
Colors past, future, and present simultaneously

key_claims: Aristotle's account leaves unanswered the question of the horizon of significance
Befindlichkeit names the existential structure; Stimmung names the ontic manifestation
Aisthesis is instantaneous; Stimmung pervades all temporal ecstases
Mood is not a psychological state but an existential condition of disclosure
notes: Contains Table 2 (aisthesis vs Stimmung). The transition paragraph is critical — it identifies the gap in Aristotle that Heidegger fills. This unit establishes Tension #3 (phantasia vs mood) and Tension #4 (form-reception vs meaning-constitution).
